definition: A small deposit that reserves a unit before the SPA is signed. It is normally deducted from your 10% down payment. Read the booking form for when it is refundable.
The contract between you and the developer. For licensed housing projects it follows a fixed government form: Schedule G for landed homes and Schedule H for strata units such as condos.
The part of the price you pay yourself, usually 10% on signing the SPA. The bank loan covers the rest.
For a project under construction, the developer bills in stages as work is completed (foundation, structure, walls, and so on). Your bank pays each bill from your loan.
Handover of the keys once the unit is complete, with water and electricity connected and a CCC issued.
Confirms the building was completed according to approved plans and is fit to occupy. Needed before VP.
After VP, the period in which the developer must repair defects you report. Under the Schedule H SPA it is 24 months.
Compensation the developer pays if it hands over late. The statutory SPA sets it at 10% a year of the purchase price for the days of delay.
The floor area of the unit as stated by the developer, in square feet. It usually includes walls and balcony.
Price divided by built-up. Use it to compare units of different sizes or projects.
A unit split into two parts with separate doors, so you can live in one and rent out the other, or rent both.
Units reserved for Bumiputera buyers, usually with a discount. Other buyers can purchase them only if the state releases the quota.
The law that licenses developers and protects buyers of new homes. Your payments go into an HDA account the developer can draw on only as the rules allow.
You own the land title with no expiry date.
You own the property for a fixed term, typically 99 years, after which the lease must be renewed with the state for a premium.
The title for a unit in a building or gated scheme with shared common property. You own your unit plus a share of the common areas.
The title for a landed home where you own the house and land outright.
Condos usually sit on residential land. Many serviced residences sit on commercial land, which can mean higher utility tariffs and assessment rates.
A high-rise home often built on commercial land, with facilities managed like a condo. Check the title type and utility rates.
The owners' body that manages the building after the developer hands over. It sets the maintenance fee and enforces house rules.
Monthly charges for security, cleaning and facilities, shared by share units. The sinking fund, at least 10% of the charges, is saved for major repairs.
Quit rent is an annual tax to the state land office. Assessment is paid to the local council, usually twice a year.
Approval from the state authority needed for every purchase by a foreigner, and for some leasehold transfers. Your lawyer applies for it.
The share of the price the bank lends. For individuals, Bank Negara caps it at 70% from the third outstanding housing loan.
Your total monthly debt repayments divided by your net income. Banks use it to decide how much you can borrow; each bank sets its own limit.

aka: Overnight Policy Rate / Standardised Base Rate
definition: The OPR is Bank Negara's policy rate. The SBR follows it, and floating home loan rates are set as SBR plus the bank's own spread.
A loan linked to a current account. Money you park in it reduces the interest charged, and you can withdraw it again.
You can pay extra to cut interest and withdraw the excess, usually with a notice period or a fee.
A basic loan with fixed monthly instalments. Extra payments reduce the balance but can't be withdrawn.
The first years of the loan, often 3 to 5, during which settling or refinancing incurs a penalty, commonly a percentage of the loan.
Insurance that pays off the loan if the borrower dies or becomes totally and permanently disabled. Cover falls as the loan balance falls. Usually paid once and can be added to the loan.
Like MRTA, but the cover stays at a fixed amount and the policy can usually move with you to another property. Premiums are higher and paid regularly.
The bank's assessment of the property's value. The loan is based on the lower of the price and the valuation.
Replacing your loan with a new one, to get a lower rate or to cash out equity. Check the lock-in penalty and the new legal and stamp duty costs.
Housing loans for civil servants, with their own margin and rate rules.
Tax on the property transfer. Malaysians and PRs pay 1% on the first RM 100k, 2% to RM 500k, 3% to RM 1M and 4% above. Foreign buyers pay a flat 8% on residential property from 1 January 2026.
0.5% of the loan amount, charged on the loan agreement.
Set by the Solicitors' Remuneration Order 2023, charged separately for the SPA and the loan agreement, plus service tax and disbursements. Developers often offer “free legal fees” packages.
Malaysian first-time buyers can get stamp duty relief on homes up to a set price. The limit and deadline change with each Budget, so check the current terms.
Tax on the gain when you sell. Malaysians pay 30% in the first 3 years, 20% in year 4, 15% in year 5 and 0% from year 6. Foreigners pay 30% within 5 years and 10% after.
Out-of-pocket costs your lawyer pays for you, such as searches, registration and courier fees, billed on top of legal fees.
The purchase price written in the Sale and Purchase Agreement. It is the price shown on this website, and the bank loan and stamp duty are based on it.
